doc.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Joining Nat Adderley's band
summary: Buddy Williams brings him into Nat Adderley's new band with Fernando Gumbs; he learns audience engagement.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: They can’t make it. Then all of a sudden it changes, he can come. But he can only come for one day. What? Then it changes, he can come for both days. So by the time Cannonball got to the campus we tried to question him about all this stuff. He said “well they told me to come for one day.” Okay. So I didn’t want to make a whole big thing or anything, but it’s something that kind of found a little spot in my brain, I found out about the attitude of the school. But moving ahead again, after college, the whole thing, then moving to Nat, because that’s when I really got to know them, Nat had formed a band. And I was asked by a very good friend and drummer Buddy Williams, to come into the band. And I also had met a bass player whose last name was the same as mine, Gumbs, Fernando. So I called him to audition on bass. So he got the gig so we were both in the band. And I stayed in the band for about maybe a year. What I learned with Nat was the importance of engaging the audience, which his brother was a master of boy. And it was so incredible to see how he was able to have the audience in the palm of his hand. And it stayed with me, as it has stayed with people like George Duke, who went through Cannonball’s band. And again we were in there for a while and then we broke up. Because he was giving us a lot of responsibility as a band. We were called Nat Adderley © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -12-
